method: These are synthetic review fixtures, not diagnoses of a specific add-on. Give a fresh evaluator only the selected prompt and input, the skill path, and available tools. Review-only cases must not modify an add-on. Keep reviewer assertions withheld. Grade decisions and proposed checks, not matching wording. Missing client/image access must remain explicit. These cases supplement the historical build evals; they do not inherit their pass status.

positive: Fix the clipped selected text in my WoW addon dropdown.
Review why this Forever addon reports a session gap after loading a zone.
Make this Retail addon panel animation smoother without changing its design.

cases.prompt: Review this proposed settings polish against the approved revision. Do not implement yet. Describe what to inspect and what would justify acceptance.
cases.input: The old plan requested a large themed window. The latest accepted revision requests compact familiar controls, readable game text, and short functional labels. The proposal follows the old plan, adds a tagline, uses a thin fixed desktop font, and shows a browser preview with substitute native artwork. No current reference images or client capture are available in this fixture.
assertions: Uses the latest accepted revision; does not restart the old design or implement during review.
Identifies font/control-density/copy mismatches without prescribing a universal panel size or aesthetic.
Calls for actual reference pixels and native font/control inspection, and explicitly does not claim to have inspected unavailable images.

cases.prompt: Review this resized dropdown and expandable panel. Explain likely defects and useful regression checks.
cases.input: The selected template text inherits TOPLEFT/TOPRIGHT anchors and a short height. The add-on only increases its height and font size. The mock text starts vertically centered with no anchors. The panel width is 70% of the screen, always expands upward, and adds a physical notch inset after anchoring inside an already inset UIParent. The whole panel uses the highest stratum and faded detail buttons remain mouse-enabled.
assertions: Traces text clipping to inherited geometry and requires a source-derived mock plus native rendering checks, rather than merely shrinking text.
Proposes bounded content width, scale-aware available-space fitting of the expanded footprint, and removal of duplicate safe-area adjustment.
Accounts for menus/system dialogs, inherited layering, and hidden hit regions without escalating every frame to the highest layer.

cases.prompt: Review this motion callback and suggest a focused optimization and validation plan. The transition must stay interruptible.
cases.input: OnUpdate advances progress by elapsed/duration, then calls RebuildLayout, SetFont, SetText, GetStringWidth, ClearAllPoints and ApplyGeometry. Opening while closing resets progress to zero. Completion leaves OnUpdate attached. A test advances only in equal 1/60-second steps; a report labels fewer mock calls as higher in-game FPS.
assertions: Recognizes that elapsed-time progress alone does not bound per-frame work.
Moves invariant preparation/measurement out of the callback with input-based invalidation, preserves current progress on reversal, and removes idle work.
Checks equal elapsed time at varied cadences, jitter and long frames while preserving intermediate motion; does not equate call counts to native FPS.

cases.prompt: Review this default-font migration and unavailable-rate display policy before implementation.
cases.input: A migration replaces every saved font/size equal to the previous default and assigns enabled = saved.enabled or true. Old profiles do not record whether defaults were explicitly selected. A profile copy omits positions. Empty, warming-up, expired and incomplete measurements all render 0 with the same tooltip; large values are shortened without an exact-value view.
assertions: Preserves false and valid profile values, makes migration repeatable, and identifies ambiguous old-default provenance without pretending intent is recoverable.
Requires profile copies to preserve applicable user preferences and records explicit choices going forward where needed.
Separates actual zero from unavailable states, uses concise contextual explanations and precise tooltip values/units.

cases.prompt: Investigate this report at review scope. What is established, and what should be checked next?
cases.input: The documented timer policy counts connected elapsed time and preserves the session across normal loading. The only code excerpt is: if now - lastTick > limit then incomplete = true end. Tests pass thousands of assertions using only punctual timer callbacks. A user reports an incomplete-data warning after a zone load. No runtime event trace, clock samples, or surrounding accounting code are supplied.
assertions: Identifies unsupported inference in the excerpt while avoiding a definitive diagnosis of the live report.
Separates delayed callbacks, ordinary elapsed time, loading, reload and disconnect; requests or proposes discriminating traces and scenario tests.
Does not simply raise the threshold, discard accumulated state, or claim passing tests prove the live report fixed.
Accounts for clock origins, recovery timestamps and client-controlled SavedVariables persistence when proposing durable-state checks.

cases.prompt: Review resource behavior and the strength of this performance claim.
cases.input: Every panel reopen constructs frames, registers callbacks and creates a ticker; closing hides the frames only. Rolling history appends one record per event forever. A test repeats one cycle, forces GC and reports stable Lua bytes. The proposed fix discards all pending events whenever the queue exceeds ten, regardless of the accounting window. No native profiler results are available.
assertions: Finds retained frame/work ownership and unbounded history despite stable Lua memory.
Proposes reuse, cancellation/reconciliation and semantic history/queue bounds that preserve valid bursts and accounting.
Checks warmup plus repeated workload windows, active events/timers, created objects and retained data separately; limits conclusions to measured evidence.
